solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old man in mine, he is unable to regularly take hard work

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
someone who is unable to do something can't, written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means keeping every other letter of the word hard

parts.note: an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: A sentence about an elderly miner too frail to keep up with heavy labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly take' keeps the first and third letters of 'hard', giving HR.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct ape-man of Java was an early human ancestor, so an 'old man' in the prehistoric sense.

clue.text: In favour of philosopher no one thanks over forecast

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a Gnostic was a follower of an early mystical religious philosophy

indicators.note: over means the following words are turned backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone backs a thinker who gives no thanks for a forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns round NO, I and TA together; TA is British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognostication is a prediction of what is to come.

clue.text: Short king with gold for teacher

parts.note: Tutankhamun is often shortened to Tut
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A monarch of little height swaps his gold for a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' means abbreviated name, not small in height.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher or one who instructs small groups.

clue.text: Runny brie consumed when drunk

indicators.note: runny cheese loses its shape, so the letters of brie are rearranged

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Runny brie eaten while tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebriate is a rare word for intoxicated, as in its relative inebriated.

clue.text: Lincoln meets fat French cleric

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's familiar name
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: Abraham Lincoln meets a portly French priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Abelard was a twelfth-century French theologian and churchman, famous for his love for Héloïse.

clue.text: Three-nation stand

parts.note: ter is the Latin combining form for three times, as in tercentenary
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A grandstand built for three countries at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Terraces are the stepped standing areas at football grounds, so a stand.

clue.text: Unusual crunched cheese dish

parts.note: rare means unusual
bit is the past tense of bite, so crunched

explanation.surface: An unusual cheese dish that was crunched up.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese on toast, a British cheese dish.

clue.text: Boris, perhaps, taking rope to Alaska

parts.note: a pastern was an old word for a rope hobbling a horse by the leg
AK is the US postal abbreviation for Alaska

explanation.surface: Boris heading off to Alaska with a length of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boris' suggests a politician; it is Boris Pasternak, the Russian author of Doctor Zhivago.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Pasternak is an example of someone named Boris, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Food is served up after holy man becomes exhausted in former capital

indicators.note: after places the food after the other pieces

parts.note: a saint is a holy man
a supply that peters out becomes exhausted

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means written upwards, backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: A saint gets food when worn out in an old capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'served up' reads the food upwards; 'after' puts it last. 'Peters' as in peters out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian city was the imperial capital until Moscow took over in 1918.

clue.text: Coats, for example, being dated, we are modelling to get right

parts.note: something out of fashion is out

indicators.note: modelling shapes material into a new form, so the letters of we are are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion show where old-fashioned coats are being modelled to get them right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelling' is the anagram signal for WE ARE, not a catwalk show.
explanation.definitionFit: Coats are garments worn over everything else, the typical example of clothing for the outside.

clue.text: No introduction of butter in cooked bistro dish

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no here means without, so a letter is taken away from the word bistro
the introduction of a word is its opening letter, here of butter

explanation.surface: A bistro dish cooked without any butter going in.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the B of 'butter' from BISTRO leaves ISTRO, which 'cooked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss grated-potato cake is a familiar dish, often served in bistros.

clue.text: Embraced by grandmother, Queen Victoria returned in a blissful state

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside, so one piece sits within the word for grandmother

parts.note: nana is a familiar name for a grandmother

indicators.note: returned means the cipher is read backwards

parts.note: VRI, Victoria Regina et Imperatrix, was Queen Victoria's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A grandmother hugging a returning Queen Victoria, both in raptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reads Victoria's cipher backwards before 'Embraced by' puts it inside the grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the state of perfect peace and release, used loosely for any bliss.

clue.text: In the air, uncertain when girl will have left

indicators.note: a person who has left is gone, so the girl's name is removed from the longer word

parts.note: being ambivalent means having mixed feelings, so uncertain
Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie

explanation.surface: Plans are up in the air and uncertain once a girl has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking VAL out of AMBIVALENT leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes the surrounding atmosphere, as in ambient temperature or noise all around.

clue.text: Large bird in Truro cathedral

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words Truro cathedral

explanation.surface: A big bird perched in the Cornish cathedral at Truro.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Truro' and the start of 'cathedral'.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is the gigantic mythical bird of the Arabian Nights, strong enough to carry elephants.

clue.text: Laver perhaps as selected player held in respect? On the contrary

indicators.note: held in means one piece goes inside another
on the contrary reverses the stated roles, so the respect goes inside the player rather than the player inside respect

parts.note: in tennis a seed is a player selected and ranked before the draw
awe is deep respect

explanation.surface: Rod Laver, the tennis great, as a seeded player held in respect.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Rod Laver the tennis star; 'On the contrary' flips 'held in', so the respect goes inside the player.
explanation.definitionFit: Laver is an edible seaweed, used in Welsh laverbread, so it is an example.

clue.text: Dessert's earlier temperature has become cold; this upset could throw plans into confusion

definitions.text: this upset could throw plans into confusion

indicators.note: has become signals that one letter changes into another

parts.note: an apple tart is a dessert
T is short for temperature; earlier picks the first of the two Ts

explanation.surface: A dessert gone cold, so the plans for dinner are upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'upset the apple cart' means to ruin plans; the first T of APPLE TART changes to C.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset the applecart is an idiom for spoiling arrangements.

clue.text: One from Genesis that has an echo just the same

indicators.text: has an echo just the same
indicators.note: an echo sending the name straight back unchanged shows that it reads the same either way

parts.note: the first woman named in the Book of Genesis

explanation.surface: A member of the band Genesis whose voice echoes back unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genesis' could be the rock band; it is the Bible book.
explanation.definitionFit: The first woman appears in the Book of Genesis as Adam's wife.

clue.text: In French red wine, English find friendly relations

parts.note: en is French for in
tent is a deep-red Spanish wine used as communion wine

explanation.surface: Diplomacy over red wine, where an Englishman and the French get along.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a dark Spanish red wine, an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is an understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale of Britain and France.

clue.text: Pinch tot

definitions.meaning: to pinch is to squeeze sharply between fingers
a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.definitionFit: A pinch and a tot of whisky are both senses of this short word.

clue.text: One thousand were sitting, set as a task

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
models who posed were sitting for an artist

explanation.surface: A thousand candidates were sitting an exam set as a task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'were sitting' means sitting for a portrait, not an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imposed is placed on someone as a duty or burden, like a task given.

clue.text: Italy to engage men first, its own men

indicators.note: first puts the other two pieces before Italy

parts.note: to sign someone is to engage them
OR, other ranks, means men in the army
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Italy signing up soldiers first from its own men.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Italian plural of signore, the title for men, in Italy's own language.

clue.text: Oil is hot for fraternity member

parts.note: derv is diesel fuel oil for road vehicles in Britain
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A frat-house member gets slick oil when it is hot.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is British for diesel fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A dervish belongs to a Sufi Muslim religious brotherhood.

clue.text: Second stop in NCP, say, by learner with electronic dash

parts.note: NCP is a big British car-park operator, so stopping in one is to park
L is the learner-driver plate
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A learner driver stopping in a car park for a second before a dash.
explanation.walkthrough: NCP, National Car Parks, is a chain of car parks across Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkle and dash both mean lively flair or verve in someone's manner.

clue.text: Rise of leading Tory moderates simmering here?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the letters are read upward, backwards

parts.note: top means leading, as in top people
wets was the Thatcher-era insult for moderate Conservatives

explanation.surface: Tory moderates rising in the party, with tempers simmering.
explanation.walkthrough: WETS: moderate Tories mocked by Thatcher's supporters in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewpot is a pot for slow cooking, where a stew simmers.

clue.text: Measure of acidity in a once lost instrument

indicators.note: in places the acidity measure inside the phrase meaning once lost

parts.note: lorn is an archaic word for lost or forsaken
pH is the scale of acidity

explanation.surface: A chemistry measurement taken in an instrument once lost.
explanation.walkthrough: LORN is a poetic, archaic word, hence 'once'; the instrument is the Swiss alpine horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The long wooden horn of the Swiss Alps is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Devour repasts regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at fixed intervals, the even-placed ones of repasts

explanation.surface: Someone who gobbles their meals on a regular schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour is to consume food greedily, a strong synonym.

clue.text: Archdeacon in terrible rage gets one retaliating

indicators.note: in places the archdeacon's title inside the jumbled rage
terrible signals that the letters of rage are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A churchman flies into a terrible rage and takes revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' makes AGER from RAGE; an archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone retaliating takes revenge for a wrong, which is what an avenger does.

clue.text: Supposes former exercise before court succeeded

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
PE is physical education, school exercise
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that an old workout before court went well.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect something is to suppose or assume it will be the case.

clue.text: Limit religious teaching in island

parts.note: a cap is a limit, as on spending
RI is religious instruction in British schools

explanation.surface: A cap placed on religious education on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: In this state I had to return nothing

indicators.note: to return means the word had is read backwards

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having to come back with nothing in some US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gem State in the north-western US, the 'state' the clue points at.

clue.text: Ad-lib production of optimum PR

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of the material, here the letters of optimum PR

explanation.surface: Public relations at its best is made up on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something done spontaneously, without preparation or rehearsal.

clue.text: Despite having to sit, presumably?

definitions.meaning: despite means in spite of, regardless
split into three words it describes a place with no standing room, so everyone must sit

explanation.surface: A grudging seat taken despite the need to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second definition as NOT WITH STANDING: no standing allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: This long word is a formal preposition meaning in spite of.
